## Summary

Recover the viewer's pane ownership and source fade queues.

```text
card → detail: transfer the same preview; fade/delete card shells
Back → cards: create fresh previews; fade/delete old detail
Update: input flags → signed alpha step → later normalization/deletion
```

## Evidence

- **Before:** the incremental branch had no pane/fade model; the preserved helper changed input early and clamped decimal alpha.
  **After:** seven source regressions fail against that helper and pass with queue-only show/hide and the existing signed8.8 display-value model.
- Formatting, TypeScript,554 rule/parser tests (6,512 assertions) and production build pass. Ten new cases protect ownership transfer, fresh Back/page/detail previews, queue reversal, neighbor deferral, overshoot/normalization and synchronous pending deletion during rapid Back.
- Pane ownership matches original47c7fa1 byte-for-byte. Decompiled _-KT/_-Lv and pcode confirm detach/push only; Update changes mouseEnabled and increments forward after splice. Delete fades retain flags until their disposal callback.
- Alpha reuses the project's display-values model, supported by Ruffle Fixed8 implementation evidence. Controlled Adobe runtime equality remains unproven. Later code-entry cancellation and local provenance/save work remain separate backlog slices.
- No current browser flow consumes these pure models. Live pane/artwork/input wiring, caller-specific flags and complete viewer/game parity remain pending. No browser server, profile, media, generated-data or simulation changes.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

Revert removes unconnected models/tests. No migration.

**Blast Radius:** viewer

Adds pure state/ownership logic.
